questions.q: In what year did Powerball hold its very first drawing?
questions.explain: Powerball's first drawing was on April 22, 1992. A player from Indiana won the $5.9 million jackpot.

questions.q: Mega Millions launched in 1996 under a different name. What was it called?
questions.explain: It ran as "The Big Game" starting in 1996 before being rebranded Mega Millions in 2002.

questions.q: What are the odds of matching all numbers to win the Powerball jackpot (current 69/26 format)?
questions.explain: About 1 in 292.2 million, based on Powerball's current 69 white-ball / 26 red-ball matrix in place since 2015.

questions.q: What is the largest lottery jackpot ever won in U.S. history?
questions.explain: A single ticket sold in Altadena, California won the record $2.04 billion Powerball jackpot on November 7, 2022.

questions.q: The largest Mega Millions jackpot ever won ($1.602 billion, August 2023) was sold in which state?
questions.explain: The winning ticket was sold in Florida, and the winner chose the roughly $794.2 million cash option.

questions.q: How many U.S. states do not sell any state lottery tickets at all?
questions.explain: Five states currently have no state lottery: Alabama, Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, and Utah.

questions.q: Which of these states does NOT have a state lottery?
questions.explain: Utah is one of only five U.S. states with no state lottery, alongside Alabama, Alaska, Hawaii, and Nevada.

questions.q: How many white balls does Powerball currently draw its five main numbers from?
questions.explain: Powerball has drawn its five main numbers from a pool of 69 white balls since the October 2015 format change.

questions.q: Mega Millions relaunched with a new format in April 2025. What did the ticket price become?
questions.explain: The April 2025 relaunch raised the ticket price to $5 and set a $50 million starting jackpot.

questions.q: In Pick 3 and Pick 4 games, what does an add-on like "Fireball" generally do?
options: Draws one extra bonus digit that can substitute into your numbers for more ways to match
Only applies to jackpot games like Powerball
questions.explain: Add-ons like Fireball draw one extra digit that can be swapped in for one of your picked digits, creating more ways to match — it doesn't change your odds of the base draw itself.

questions.q: What was the winning amount of the very first Powerball jackpot in 1992?
questions.explain: The first Powerball jackpot was $5.9 million, won by a player from Indiana.

questions.q: In what year was "The Big Game" rebranded as Mega Millions?
questions.explain: The rebrand to Mega Millions happened in 2002.
